title: Trust package: RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export — customer questionnaire scaffold
content:
Purpose and scope:
This draft is a customer-facing trust package scaffold that summarizes: RBAC v2 (roles, groups, delegations), the current audit log schema and retention options, SIEM export capabilities (formats and delivery patterns), and our evidence automation approach for security questionnaires. Use this doc as the single-pane summary for Security/CS teams when responding to inbound customer questionnaires and for populating the Trust Center page.

Status and intent:
- Current status: in_review.
- Audience: Customer security reviewers, sales engineering, compliance reviewers.
- Not a formal policy. Links to authoritative artifacts (Confluence, PRs, JIRA) are included for controls and implementation details.

Executive summary (high-level answers for questionnaires):
- RBAC v2: Redwood Inference supports role-based access control with first-class support for fine-grained roles, team/group mappings, and temporary delegated access. Roles map to permissions that are versioned and stored in the control plane. Customers can request role exports or pin a custom role set in Private/Dedicated deployments.
- Audit logs: We capture immutable, append-only audit logs for control plane actions, model deployments, API key lifecycle events, admin actions, and data plane accesses. Logs include standardized fields (timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource, outcome, request_id, ip, user_agent) and are cryptographically integrity-protected in Dedicated/Private.
- SIEM export: We support push-based export (secure syslog/TCP TLS), and cloud-native delivery (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/JSON to S3) with configurable formats: JSON (preferred), CEF, and LEEF. Customers can also request a streaming webhook with HMAC authentication for partner SIEMs.
- Evidence automation: We provide a repeatable evidence-bundler that collects logs, role matrices, configuration snapshots, and signed certificates into time-stamped bundles for questionnaire evidence packages. This is integrated with our policy-as-code test suites so that evidence is generated from the current state, not stale docs.

RBAC v2: implementation notes (for SEs answering details)
- Role model: role -> permission set -> scope (org, project, model). Hierarchical scoping supported (organizational, workspace, project).
- Delegation: temporary role grants (timeboxed tokens) and just-in-time approval flows (integration with Okta/IdP via SCIM + OIDC).
- Separation of duties: admin vs billing vs inference-operator roles are distinct; customers can create custom roles.
- Export: we can export a CSV/JSON of current role bindings for the last 90 days on hosted plan, longer on Dedicated/Private.
- Common questionnaire Q: "How do you prevent privilege escalation?" Suggested answer: "RBAC v2 enforces least-privilege roles by default; admin operations require 2-step approval or MFA for changes to role assignments. All role-changes are audited and reversible via role-binding history."

Audit log schema (concise reference for CS answers)
- Standard fields (present in every event):
  - event_timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
  - event_id: UUID v4
  - request_id: traceable request correlation id
  - actor_id: internal user id or service principal
  - actor_type: human | service | api_key | system
  - action: short verb (e.g., deploy_model, api_key.create, user.login, role.update)
  - resource_type: model | deployment | key | role | config
  - resource_id: opaque id (customer-visible if applicable)
  - outcome: success | failure | partial
  - ip_address: source IPv4/IPv6
  - user_agent: client UA or SDK identifier
  - metadata: freeform JSON payload (string-escaped for exports) — used for diff snapshots or stack traces

- Integrity and tamper-evidence:
  - Hosted: logs are write-once in append stores with immutability windows and TTL per plan.
  - Dedicated/Private: option to enable signed log segments (SHA256 tree-hash) and export of signatures for customer archival.

- Retention and access:
  - Default retention: 90 days for hosted.
  - Extended retention: configurable up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private with contractual SLAs.
  - Access: role-gated downloads via console + audit trail of who downloaded.

SIEM export and formats (practical implementation):
- Delivery modes supported: syslog over TLS (RFC 5425), HTTPS webhook with HMAC, S3 JSON batches, and cloud-native sink connectors.
- Formats: JSON (flat events), CEF (mapping provided), LEEF (mapping provided). Mapping tables live in Confluence.
- Throughput: streaming exports are typically batched to 2–10s windows for cost efficiency; customers can request near-realtime (sub-second) streaming for critical alerts.
- Failure/retry: exponential backoff with DLQ to S3 for up to 30 days; alerting to customer owner on persistent failures.

Evidence automation: how it works and common outputs
- evidence-bundler (internal name): collects
  1) role_binding_snapshot.csv (roles, members, timestamps)
  2) audit_log_slice.json.gz (time-windowed, signed if requested)
  3) config_snapshot.yaml (RBAC config, network allowlists, SIEM endpoints)
  4) deployment_manifest.txt (model versions, runtime image digests)
  5) signed_statement.txt (SRE/Compliance attestation)
- Bundles are time-stamped and checksum-signed with our key. For Dedicated/Private customers we can produce keys they bring (BYOK) and provide attestations.
- Typical lead time: automated bundle generation takes 10–30 minutes for 90 days of logs (depends on retention window and plan).

Customer questionnaire snippets (copy-paste friendly)
Q: Do you capture administrative and data access events?
A: Yes. Administrative operations (role changes, policy updates, service account management) and data-plane operations (model deployments, inference requests metadata, API key usage) are recorded. Event schemas include timestamps, actor identifiers, outcome, and request correlation IDs for end-to-end tracing.

Q: Can we receive audit logs directly into our SIEM?
A: Yes. We support push (syslog over TLS), webhook streaming with HMAC, and cloud-sink exports (S3/Cloud Storage). Supported formats: JSON (recommended), CEF, LEEF. Configure export via Console > Security > Log Exports or request a Managed Export setup for Dedicated contracts.

Q: How do you ensure the integrity of audit logs?
A: For Dedicated/Private customers we support signed log segments with a verifiable chain (SHA256 tree-hash). Hosted plans use write-once append stores and operational controls; integrity keys and signed digests are available on request for compliance reviews.

Operational runbook notes (internal):
- Owners: Security (Priya), SRE (Ethan) for export pipelines, Product (Marta) for Console UX.
- Known gaps / TODOs:
  - Confluence page needs an updated CEF/LEEF field mapping (SEC-412).
  - Evidence-bundler needs UI dropdown for time-window presets (PR under review).
  - Clarify retention for API key usage events in hosted - action item: product to propose policy.

Notes and guidance for CS/Sales engineers when sharing with customers:
- Default to the short questionnaire snippets above. If a customer requests cryptographic proofs or longer retention than standard, escalate to Security (Priya) and SRE (Ethan).
- Avoid sharing raw logs publicly; package them via evidence-bundler and redact PII if requested.
- For Private deployments, customers may request local archivist access and key export; legal/ops must sign an addendum.

Unresolved questions (for internal follow-up):
- Do we ship signed digests for hosted customers as a paid add-on? (product decision)
- Clarify default retention for API key telemetry (current default ambiguous in codebase).

References and next steps:
- Confluence: RBAC v2 Design (link above).
- PR: platform/pull/1287 (evidence-bundler enhancements).
- Linear: SEC-412 (CEF mapping) and SEC-421 (retention policy clarity).

End of draft.
